title: Quantum Simulation of Spin-Dependent Electron Transfer in a Synthetic Chiral Lattice with a Trapped Ion
authors: Yi Li, Chuyuan Chen, Xingyu Zhao, Zihan Xie, Min Jiang, Xinhua Peng, Han Pu, Lyuzhou Ye, Yao Wang, Guozhen Zhang, Yiheng Lin
abstract: Electron transfer through chiral structures can exhibit spin asymmetry, known as the chiral-induced spin selectivity effect, whose microscopic origin remains an open question. While path-interference within the chiral moiety has been proposed as a key mechanism, its experimental validation requires precise and versatile tunability of system parameters. Here we implement a programmable quantum simulation of spin-dependent electron transfer in a donor--chiral-bridge--acceptor model using a trapped ion. The bridge is encoded in internal states of the ion with tunable nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor couplings, while donor and acceptor states are coupled via a spectator bosonic motional mode. We observe spin-dependent interference within the bridge, and further reveal spin-dependence in donor-to-acceptor transfer dynamics, controlled by amplitude and phase of the coupling parameter. Our results identify interference among spin-dependent pathways as a microscopic origin of spin-dependent transfer, and open a route toward quantum simulations of complex chiral lattices with multi-level and bosonic degrees of freedom.
summary: The authors successfully implemented a programmable quantum simulation of spin-dependent electron transfer using a trapped ion platform. They modeled the process through a synthetic chiral lattice bridge connecting donor and acceptor sites. The key finding is that spin selectivity arises from quantum interference between multiple competing pathways, providing a robust experimental route to study CISS effects.
main_problem: The study addresses the unresolved microscopic origin of the Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) effect in electron transfer through chiral structures.
main_result: The research identifies that spin-dependent interference among competing multi-step pathways within the synthetic chiral bridge is the microscopic mechanism responsible for observing spin-selective electron transport.
method: A programmable quantum simulation approach was implemented using a single trapped ion to model the donor–chiral bridge–acceptor system dynamics.
model_or_system: The system models $	ext{D}–	ext{B}_\chi–	ext{A}$ electron transfer, where the chiral bridge is encoded across four sites ($|	ext{B}_1angle$ to $|	ext{B}_4angle$) on a trapped $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ion. The couplings are tunable using laser and RF drives, simulating nearest-neighbor hopping and spin-dependent next-nearest-neighbor interactions.
key_observables: Spin polarization ($P$), population distribution across bridge sites ($	ext{|B}_2angle, 	ext{|B}_3angle, 	ext{|B}_4angle$), and the overall donor-to-acceptor transfer dynamics over time.
important_parameters: Hopping strengths ($t_j$), SOC strength ($\lambda$), phase ($\phi$), and coupling amplitudes/phases. Key regimes include $\lambda/t$ ratios and specific time windows (e.g., $200–300 \mu	ext{s}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes coherent evolution over specified time windows, and the mechanism relies on interference terms derived from path summation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental scheme (Hamiltonian structure, laser implementation), show spin-dependent time evolution within the chiral bridge, and demonstrate tunable spin polarization in both the bridge dynamics and the final donor-to-acceptor transfer.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model Hamiltonian for $	ext{D}–	ext{B}_\chi–	ext{A}$ on a trapped ion. It then analyzes the intrinsic spin-dependent interference within the chiral bridge, followed by extending this analysis to measure the resulting spin selectivity during the full donor-to-acceptor transfer process.
why_interesting: This work provides an unprecedentedly controllable quantum simulator platform for studying complex solid-state phenomena like CISS. The ability to tune parameters ($\lambda/t$, $\phi$) allows direct mapping of theoretical predictions regarding interference mechanisms onto measurable quantum dynamics, which is highly valuable for AMO research into open quantum systems.
